Add the no-worker-identifiers rule and its email check (#292)

Add the adopter-owned rule under .claude/rules/external/ that bars any
worker email address, account identifier, seat label or other
third-party identifier from every public or potentially public
surface, and link it from the Adopted governance section of
.claude/CLAUDE.md.

Add tools/test-no-worker-identifiers.py, which reads the raw bytes of
every regular file that git ls-files lists (a tracked symbolic link
and a submodule are not read) and takes every candidate address
around every at sign, so an exempt candidate cannot hide another, with
work that grows linearly with the file. The maintainer's own address
and the reserved documentation domains are exempt, and 1 exact-line
allowlist entry covers the URL-userinfo fixture in
tools/test-release-links.py; a stale entry fails. A failure names the
file, the line number and a digest of the match, never its text. A
failed git call, a git that cannot start, a missing file or an
unreadable file fails closed. Each caught example in the suite is
assembled at run time, so its source holds no matchable text.

Run the suite as a named step of the Orchestration registry workflow,
name it in the header of that workflow, mirror it in
tools/run_all_checks.sh, and record the new sha256 of that script in
tools/test-run-all-checks.py, which pins it.

Residual: the check covers the email class only. Seat labels, bare
handles and numeric account identifiers rest on the rule itself, and
a surface that is not a file, such as a pull request description, is
not reached.
